title: Manchester United's new boss inherits a long, urgent to-do list
body:
Manchester United have agreed a deal to make Mauricio Pochettino their next head coach [S2]. Sky Sports reports the agreement as a two-and-a-half-year contract [S2].

BBC Sport has framed his in-tray around three issues: culture, defence and Bruno Fernandes [S1]. Each is a different kind of headache, and they are not easy to solve in isolation. A culture problem can hide a defensive one, and a midfield question can make both worse.

The league record shows why those issues are urgent. Over their last five league matches, Manchester United have taken 3 points, with no wins, three draws and two defeats [ST1]. They have scored 6 goals and conceded 11 [ST1].

That run reads like a side that has become easy to hit and hard to trust. The sequence matters as much as the totals: draws, then defeats, with nothing to build on. The new man inherits a defence that has been leaking and a dressing room that needs a reason to believe again.

The new coach's first job is to stop the bleeding, not to chase a grand plan. Give the appointment time, but judge it quickly on whether the goals against start to fall.

The Touchline Take: one to keep an eye on as the season unfolds, because the to-do list is longer than the headline suggests.
